RED-FLAGS REPORT — DILIGENCE REVIEW
Prairie Aerostructures Holdings
Engagement: Aerospace Vertical Integration — Counterparty Markup Reconciliation

SCOPE AND SOURCES.
This red-flags report reconciles the counterparty's latest markup against the base diligence materials for the Prairie Aerostructures Holdings engagement, incorporating the disclosure schedules/exhibits and the controlling deal-team instructions. Four operative sources were reviewed in full: (i) base deal materials, (ii) counterparty markup, (iii) schedules and exhibits, and (iv) deal team correspondence. One file located in the matter folder — "Unrelated correspondence — administrative file 10" — was reviewed and excluded as a misfiled distractor not to be relied upon.

CONTROLLING CLIENT INSTRUCTION.
The deal-team correspondence contains a revised priority instruction in its latest message, which controls over the superseded earlier messages. Under the controlling instruction, the client: (a) will concede the basket conversion (deductible to tipping basket), and (b) treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. The deliverable reflects the controlling instruction, not the superseded ordering.

SUMMARY OF COUNTERPARTY DEVIATIONS (MUST EACH BE ADDRESSED).

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification cap silently reduced (RED FLAG — REJECT / PUSH BACK).
The counterparty markup silently reduces the indemnification cap against the base materials. This is a material adverse shift in the allocation of indemnification risk and was not flagged as conceded. It must be rejected or negotiated back to the base level. Further, Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the markup's indemnification changes would silently shift toward the buyer/client. The scheduled exceptions control over general statements in the base materials, so this deviation must be reconciled against Schedule 5.2 and the cap restored.

DEVIATION 2 — Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket (CONCEDED PER CLIENT — MECHANICS STILL FLAGGED).
The counterparty markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Under the controlling client instruction this conversion is conceded and is not a walk-away item. However, the mechanics must still be reconciled with Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities and Documented with the correct threshold treatment; it should be implemented as a clean tipping basket consistent with the conceded position.

DEVIATION 3 — Material Adverse Effect carve-outs for the exact regulatory action at issue (RED FLAG — REJECT / HIGH RISK).
The markup amends the Material Adverse Effect definition to add carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter. Schedule 3.7 discloses TWO pending regulatory inquiries that intersect these MAE carve-outs. Because the scheduled exceptions control over general statements, the carve-outs would operate to exclude the very pending-regulatory-inquiry risk disclosed in Schedule 3.7 from the definition of MAE, removing client protection on the exact exposure flagged in diligence. This is a walk-away-caliber red flag: the MAE carve-outs must be rejected or narrowed so that the disclosed Schedule 3.7 inquiries remain within (or are excluded only with compensating protection).

DEVIATION 4 — Limitation period shortens survival for core representations (WALK-AWAY ISSUE — HIGHEST PRIORITY).
The markup introduces a shortened limitation period that reduces the survival period for the core representations. This directly contradicts Exhibit B, which sets the survival matrix. Per the controlling client instruction, ANY survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. This is the highest-priority red flag and must be rejected in its entirety; the survival periods must remain at the Exhibit B levels.

RECONCILIATION SUMMARY.
- Every counterparty deviation has been identified and reconciled against the base materials, the disclosure schedules (3.7, 5.2) and Exhibit B, and the controlling deal-team instruction.
- Priority red flags: (1) survival-period reduction (walk-away), (2) MAE carve-outs intersecting Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries, (3) silent indemnification cap reduction with Schedule 5.2 interplay.
- Conceded item: basket conversion (tipping basket) — accepted per client, subject to clean mechanics.
- The distractor document (administrative file 10) was excluded from this analysis.
